projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The simultaneous increase to 17 connected devices, followed by a tight cluster of outdoor audio, impact sounds, and dog barking, strongly indicates a recent arrival or perimeter interaction that just brought someone inside. Since presence data confirms all devices are home and cameras show no alerts, this aligns with a normal late household activity, but the dogs' heightened reaction suggests a quick perimeter check if the family isn't aware of recent movement.
Unusually quiet at whole_home this hour: 0 observations vs typical 9 for weekday 21:00

The synchronized cluster of outdoor ambient sounds, repeated impact/movement noises, and dog barking between 20:30–20:33, immediately followed by a presence spike to 17 devices, strongly indicates a vehicle or visitor arrived at the perimeter just before the household settled inside. Notably, these perimeter events triggered audio sensors but no cameras, suggesting a potential coverage gap worth reviewing.
Unusually quiet at whole_home this hour: 0 observations vs typical 8 for weekday 20:00

The synchronized cluster of outdoor ambient sounds, distinct impact/movement noises, and perimeter dog barking at 19:16-19:19 strongly indicates a visitor or delivery at the entrance, despite cameras being inactive. With 17-18 devices home, the household may have missed the arrival, so a quick check of the doorbell or gate is recommended.
Unusually quiet at whole_home this hour: 0 observations vs typical 4 for weekday 19:00

The synchronized drop of 4 mobile devices in three minutes, paired with clustered outdoor audio and a sudden dog bark, indicates the family is likely departing for an evening activity. The lack of camera footage suggests a non-camera exit route (e.g., garage), which is normal but worth confirming if unplanned.
Unusually quiet at whole_home this hour: 0 observations vs typical 5 for weekday 18:00

The tight clustering of music, TV, speech, and whole-home audio spikes alongside dog barking indicates the family is actively responding to a recurring outdoor stimulus (likely a regular delivery or neighborhood activity), confirming this is a predictable daily routine rather than an anomaly.

The synchronized pattern of dog barking, whole-home audio spikes, and outdoor ambient sounds recurring at 13:11 and 16:19 points to intermittent external stimuli, such as deliveries or neighborhood activity, agitating the dogs. The absence of camera triggers during these audio events suggests the activity occurs outside the camera's field of view, but the consistent pattern indicates routine household activity rather than a security threat.
